text:
ConocoPhillips fell slightly today as oil prices retreated—US crude dropped to $89.62 per barrel, down from recent highs around $92–93 range. The stock has been volatile over the past week, hitting a peak of $142.28 on November 13 before sliding back nearly $3, suggesting investors are stepping back as near-term energy demand concerns weigh on sentiment.

The broader backdrop remains mixed for oil refiners. While heating oil prices are sharply elevated (up 59% year-over-year), which normally supports energy stocks, fresh geopolitical risks in the Middle East—Iran escalating threats as a third US carrier arrives in the Gulf—haven't been enough to sustain the rally. These regional tensions can be oil-supportive longer-term, but markets are currently focused on the immediate price pullback rather than potential supply disruptions.
